parsed.title: Discussion on tax filing, domain purchase, and app viability

claims.text: User U1 paid ~500 UAH to aunt Sveta to correct a large tax declaration error caused by mislabelled columns.
U1's inspector ignored declarations for 1.5 years and only later demanded re‑verification of all years, leading to a correct re‑submission costing about 1000 UAH.
The tax calculation procedure takes about an hour with Excel, possibly a day per month.
Quarterly reports must be filed correctly to avoid penalties.
Mistakes in column selection dramatically affect tax amounts, often by several thousand hryvnias.
U2 has not bought a domain yet.
U4 doubts buying a domain, calling it a “silly thing” that won’t be profitable.
U1 suggests that buying a tax calculator could free money for a domain.
U1 reports that web platforms are less profitable than Android/iOS, with poor SEO and no passive ad revenue.
A successful approach cited involves fast delivery (< 1 week) using a cross‑platform stack like Flutter and copying popular ideas.
U4 questions the audience size, asking if there are at least ten people willing to pay 299 UAH.
U1 wonders if the source code could be found by searching for the password.
U4 suspects the project is a scam, calling it “local‑first app” with minimal features and a hidden password for a 100 % discount.
U5 labels the offer as “pirate” and confirms it’s a scam.
U1 jokingly claims most LinkedIn users could hack the app easily.
